Around 60 per cent of Southeast Asia's crude oil imports and one-third of its natural gas imports originated from the Middle East before Feb 28.  The disruption has highlighted the risks of heavy import dependence, concentrated supply routes and limited diversification, the IEA said in its ASEAN Energy Security Review published on Monday (Oct 5). Analysts said that the current crisis is a reminder of how exposed Southeast Asia remains to external energy shocks.  “The region’s energy demand is growing rapidly, while many countries are becoming more dependent on imported oil and gas. As such, what happens in the Middle East can very quickly translate into higher energy and transport costs, inflationary pressures and concerns over supply security at home,” Joanne Lin, senior fellow and coordinator of the ASEAN Studies Centre at Singapore’s ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute, told CNA. Southeast Asia’s electricity demand is expected to grow by about 5.4 per cent a year between 2026 and 2030, driven by industrial expansion, cooling needs and the rapid development of data centres, IEA noted.  The region’s energy demand has grown by about 30 per cent per person over the past decade.

Related:

What the Iran war shows about Singapore's energy resilience for now and the future

How exposed is Southeast Asia’s energy supply to the Iran war - who is most vulnerable and what’s next?

A DEPENDENCE THAT RUNS DEEP Southeast Asia's vulnerability goes beyond its reliance on imported oil. Oil demand continues to grow while regional crude production has fallen by 40 per cent since its peak in the 1990s, increasing dependence on imported crude, which has risen by 30 per cent since 2015, the IEA report said. The region faces a broad set of interconnected energy security challenges, including rising dependence on imported oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), it added. Around 89 per cent of petroleum product demand is met by refineries within Southeast Asia. But those refineries still depend heavily on imported crude, much of it from the Middle East, the IEA said. Around 45 per cent of refined oil products in the region are derived from Middle Eastern crude. That means Southeast Asia can be exposed to Middle East disruptions even when it is not directly importing finished fuel from the region. Some refineries are also configured to process the medium and heavy crude grades commonly supplied by Gulf producers, making it harder to switch quickly to alternative sources. STOCKPILES CAN BUY TIME This week, Southeast Asian energy ministers are expected to discuss measures under the ASEAN Framework Agreement on Petroleum Security, or APSA, including how countries could coordinate during severe supply disruptions. But the region's ability to rely on emergency stocks varies widely. The IEA's review shows that some countries are still developing strategic petroleum reserves. Indonesia has a reserve framework but has not implemented it, while the Philippines is planning a strategic petroleum reserve.  Singapore does not have a strategic petroleum reserve, according to the IEA, although power generators are required to maintain diesel stocks as a backup to natural gas. The ASEAN Centre for Energy has warned that a severe disruption to Middle East supplies could put oil volumes equivalent to nearly 28 per cent of ASEAN's final oil consumption at risk. That has added urgency to proposals for regional stockpiling.

A man refuels the tank of a motorcycle at a petrol station in Manila on Apr 7, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Jam Sta Rosa)

Philippine Energy Secretary Sharon Garin has said Manila is exploring regional fuel-storage arrangements and could host future storage facilities, Reuters reported. Analysts said stockpiling serves as a buffer when there is a sudden disruption, rather than a long-term solution.  “They are … costly to build and maintain, and Southeast Asian countries have very different levels of storage capacity and fiscal resources. It may not be realistic for every country to maintain very large reserves on its own due to these reasons,” said Lin. She added that stockpiling needed to be part of a much wider approach that includes diversification, regional connectivity and better crisis preparedness. Reserves have “obvious limitations”, agreed Tan-Soo Jie Sheng, assistant professor and director of the Institute for Environment and Sustainability at Singapore’s Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. “A 30-, 60- or 90-day reserve does little for a prolonged disruption,” he said. “Stocks also require storage capacity, financing, inventory management and very clear rules on ownership and usage.” He stressed that governments also need contingency plans for managing demand. “For instance, which uses of fuel are essential, how can public transport absorb additional demand, how should vulnerable households be supported if prices rise, should support come through blanket petrol subsidies or more targeted assistance?” “Stockpiling is therefore valuable because it buys time. But buying time should not be confused with addressing the structural causes of energy vulnerability,” he warned.  The IEA said ASEAN countries can strengthen domestic oil resilience by building more robust stockholding policies, demand-side measures and clear crisis procedures. For instance, countries with domestic resources can consider how to increase production through predictable fiscal regimes that are supportive of investment, the review said. An additional issue is that many countries in the region subsidise or regulate petrol and other fuel prices, said Tan-Soo. “While this is important for protecting households, especially during a sudden price spike, the subsidy does not make the external shock disappear as it transfers the cost from household budgets to the government budget,” he said.  “And if consumers are insulated from higher prices, there is also less incentive to reduce fuel consumption when supply is tight.” The crisis has also raised questions about how quickly ASEAN's existing energy-security mechanisms can be put into practice. While member states have agreed on the principle of greater cooperation, implementing those plans can take time. Turning regional commitments into working arrangements for information sharing, emergency response and cross-border support will be increasingly important as the region’s energy needs grow, IEA said. But coordinated energy security measures “must reflect different national circumstances”. Several ASEAN countries still rely significantly on coal for power generation and industry and will need a reliable supply and ways to diversify away from it, it cited.  In 2024, coal accounted for 71 per cent of Indonesia’s electricity generation and 62.5 per cent of the Philippines’ electricity generation, according to IEA data.

LOOKING BEYOND THE NEXT CRISIS Renewable energy and electric vehicles could reduce the region's exposure to imported oil over time, while greater electricity interconnection could allow countries to share power when supplies are tight. The current crisis could accelerate that shift, analysts said. “The US-Iran conflict has shone a spotlight on Southeast Asia’s dependence on the Middle East for oil and gas,” said Ian Storey, a senior fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute. “The crisis will act as a catalyst for Southeast Asian countries to strengthen their energy security by increasing the use of renewable energy resources … and clean energy sources, especially nuclear power.”

Greater regional electricity connectivity could complement that diversification, said Alvin Chew, Senior Fellow at the S Rajaratnam School of International Studies (RSIS) in Singapore.  “It is important that the region establish a regional grid whereby there could be aggregation of regional production capacity to meet its energy demand,” he said.

“Renewable energy is one area, while nuclear will be another for the supply of baseload energy." The IEA estimates that around US$27 billion will be needed between 2025 and 2040 for the current pipeline of regional interconnection projects, roughly 14 times the investment in Southeast Asian interconnectors since the 1970s. “The region’s diverse renewable energy resource potential, including solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal and modern sustainable biomass, can support greater diversification of electricity supply while reducing exposure to imported fossil fuels,” IEA’s review stated.

This photograph taken on Jan 22, 2021 shows a worker checking a floating solar power farm at sea, off Singapore's northern coast just across the Malaysian state of Johor. (Photo: AFP/Roslan Rahman)

Measures to integrate a greater share of renewables in the energy mix are needed – flexible power plants and enhanced grid capacity, among others, IEA said.  Clean energy can strengthen security, said Peter Govindasamy, executive director of the Energy Studies Institute at the National University of Singapore.  “Renewables, efficiency, electrification, and distributed energy systems are often discussed in climate terms, but they are equally important from a security perspective. Every unit of domestic solar, wind, hydro, or geothermal generation reduces exposure to international fuel markets,” he said. Diversification means having a more diversified energy mix, investing in renewables and efficiency, strengthening grids and storage, and developing regional arrangements that can provide support during a crisis, said Lin.  “The objective should be to have more options and avoid replacing one dependency with another,” she said.  In the meantime, Southeast Asia can ease pressure on its fuel imports and power systems by having more efficient vehicles, buildings, appliances and industrial equipment, the IEA said. “Energy efficiency is often the most cost-effective means of strengthening energy security because it reduces energy demand, lowers energy expenditure, and reduces the need for energy infrastructure investment and fuel imports,” it said.

item.title: Spain, Portugal data centre boom spurs clean power, storage build
item.description: Power developers in Spain and Portugal must build day-and-night power solutions and clinch available grid points to capitalise on data centre builders lured by solar and wind.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Garcia
item.content:encoded: Abundant solar and wind resources and opportunities for grid connections have sparked a surge in data centre development in Spain and Portugal. The Iberian Peninsula will account for roughly 11.5% of installed data centre capacity in Europe by 2030, up from 5.8% in 2025, according to research group Rystad Energy. Spain's data centre capacity is forecast to rise fourfold in the next five years to reach 3.9 GW in 2030, enjoying the second largest increase in absolute terms in Europe, behind the UK. Neighbouring Portugal, which has a much smaller population, will grow faster than any other country to install over 1 GW of data centre capacity by the end of the decade, Rystad Energy predicts. Spain's capital Madrid and the northern regions of Aragon and Navarra will host the bulk of the announced pipeline, but other areas could become data centre hubs. High shares of intermittent solar and wind capacity in Spain and Portugal mean that power companies may need to invest in solutions that provide baseload or firm power supply, such as battery storage and hybrid plants, Odin Foldvik Eikeland Senior Analyst, Renewables & Power for EMEA at Rystad Energy, told Reuters Events. Renewable energy accounted for 56% of electricity generation in Spain in 2025 and over 80% in Portugal, official data from the European Commission shows. CHART: Cumulative installed capacity of data centres in Europe Source: Rystad Energy (2026) Other challenges for data centre developers in Iberia will include dwindling grid capacity in the coming years and environmental factors such as high temperatures and scarce water supplies. These headwinds will create "downside risk” for the capacity outlook, Eikeland said. Connecting in Spain Grid availability could determine where data centre developers locate facilities in Spain going forward. Roughly 70% of Spain's transmission nodes have no capacity available and data centre clusters around Madrid, Aragon – where Microsoft is investing 5.3 billion euros in three data centres – and Navarra, have little remaining headroom. Regions including Murcia, Andalucia, and Castilla y Leon show potential for grid connection availability, Eikeland said. For available grid capacity, “Spain still compares favorably with Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam or Dublin, but that gap is closing,” he noted. Equinix has six data centres in Madrid and two in Barcelona and has followed a strategy of placing its data centres inside strategic global metropolitan hubs to keep data physically close to users. “There is a lack of investments in substations, power lines, and infrastructure to bring the power generated hundreds of kilometers away from the points of consumption,” Valentín Pinuaga, Managing Director of Equinix Espana, told Reuters Events. The Spanish government last month authorized 17 billion euros ($19.6 billion) in investments in the power grid through 2030, some 30% more than initially planned. But transmission projects will take several years to materialize, in part due to ongoing supply chain bottlenecks for large power transformers, Pinagua said. Big Power As data centres prioritize access to grids and firm power supplies, large utilities such as Iberdrola, Endesa, and EDP are well positioned to capitalise. These companies are diversifying their generation portfolios away from solar in order to provide firmer power solutions, Eikeland said. Endesa is diversifying more into wind and battery storage. While Iberdrola and EDP have long-standing hydropower fleets that provide firm power, the recent rise in solar power generation means Iberdrola is diversifying into battery storage and more hydro, and EDP is developing hybrid and storage projects as well as repowering existing facilities, Eikeland said. Endesa plans 1.9 GW of new renewables by 2028, including 1.5 GW of wind plus batteries, as it seeks to move away from solar towards a more diversified generation profile. Download our exclusive report on Europe's shift to grid value technologies. Ana Quelhas, EVP Hydrogen and Data Centers at EDP Renewables, said that solar and wind will continue to play a central role in the company’s investment plans “because of the quality of the resource base and their competitiveness.” However, EDP plans to diversify its investments to maintain grid reliability and system adequacy. “That means future solutions will increasingly combine multiple technologies and capabilities, including renewable generation, storage, flexibility solutions and, where appropriate, other forms of firm capacity,” Quelhas told Reuters Events. Battery growth Battery storage will be key to ensuring the 24-hour operation of day centres. Merlin Properties, a leading data centre developer in Spain and Portugal, in February signed a 40-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with power developer Solaria for 426 MW of solar power and an additional 10-year contract for 600 MWh of battery energy storage. Solaria at the time described the deal as “the first hybrid solar and battery PPA signed in the Spanish market.” “Most important is that the region enables a strong buildout of batteries to help with the intermittent generation challenge and enables more large-scale hybrid PPA deals where the data centre developers can ensure more baseload power supply,” Eikeland said. For exclusive energy insights, sign up to our newsletter . Data centre developers must also factor in higher cooling costs and more water constraints in Spain and Portugal than in northern European countries, which has prompted many data centre developers to choose the chilly Nordic region over the Iberian Peninsula. Portugal builds Portugal has 36 operational data centres and a further 10 in construction or planning, according to Synertics, a Portuguese energy consultancy. The Lisbon area is the epicentre of the Portuguese data centre boom with nearly 1.4 GW planned, compared with just 25 MW of IT capacity currently operational. Although investments have so far been concentrated in the Lisbon and Porto metropolitan areas, “grid capacity in Portugal is more available than the market assumes,” and there are areas along existing transmission corridors that could attract data centre investments in the future, said Synertics CEO Manuel Pessanha. MAP: Data centres, high voltage transmission lines in Portugal Source: Synertics, 2026 A key project under development is Start Campus' 1.2 GW SINES data center campus in Sines, near Lisbon, currently scheduled to be completed in 2030. The facility is located at a decommissioned coal plant site and will use seawater for cooling. The first module has been up and running since early 2025 and now has 37 MW of computing capacity, much of which is provided to Microsoft through Nscale. A second 200 MW module that will come on stream in 2027 will also provide computing power to the Nscale-Microsoft collaboration, with four additional 200 MW modules slated to start operations over the next few years. Start Campus has not yet sold the additional capacity to data center developers but has a very strong pipeline from customers that want “two or more buildings,” Omer Wilson, Chief Marketing Officer of Start Campus, said. The developer has a PPA in place with EDP for the first module and a memorandum of understanding with the energy company “that allows us to look at a long roadmap of potential PPAs for the future,” Wilson said. “What we wanted to do with EDP was to look at how do can work with them on their new renewable projects to add capacity to the grid," he said. "So we will take from that added capacity in the coming years, not from the existing capacity for the population.” The partnership between Start Campus and EDP could lead to future data center projects elsewhere in Iberia. “EDP sits on a lot of solar plants and lots of different locations which could be very well suited for future data center development,” Wilson said. EDP is “actively engaging” with other data center developers and hyperscalers to build partnerships from the ground up, Quelhas said. “As projects grow larger, success depends less on negotiating a power contract at the end of the process and more on designing energy, infrastructure and demand solutions together from the beginning,” she said.

item.title: EBA-Chef warnt Europas Banken vor Selbstzufriedenheit
item.description: Europas Banken stehen nach Einschätzung des Chefs der Europäischen Bankenaufsichtsbehörde (EBA), Francois-Louis Michaud, trotz ihrer derzeit starken Ertragslage vor erheblichen Herausforderungen. Die Institute seien so profitabel wie lange nicht mehr, während die Kostenquoten gesunken seien, sagte Michaud am Dienstag bei einer Aufsichtskonferenz der österreichischen Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA) in Wien. Das positive Bild dürfe jedoch nicht zu Selbstzufriedenheit führen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europas Banken stehen nach Einschätzung des Chefs der Europäischen Bankenaufsichtsbehörde (EBA), Francois-Louis Michaud, trotz ihrer derzeit starken Ertragslage vor erheblichen Herausforderungen. Die Institute seien so profitabel wie lange nicht mehr, während die Kostenquoten gesunken seien, sagte Michaud am Dienstag bei einer Aufsichtskonferenz der österreichischen Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA) in Wien. Das positive Bild dürfe jedoch nicht zu Selbstzufriedenheit führen. "Alles sieht gut aus", sagte Michaud mit Verweis auf gestiegene Gewinne und gesunkene Kosten. Die Banken hätten von den Reformen nach der Finanzkrise, einer verbesserten Risikosteuerung und dem Ausbau der europäischen Aufsichtsarchitektur profitiert. Zugleich warnte der EBA-Chef vor einem zunehmend unsicheren Umfeld. Hohe Staatsschulden, geopolitische Spannungen sowie mögliche Belastungen bei Kreditqualität und Betriebskosten könnten die Erträge künftig unter Druck setzen. Zudem seien die Bewertungen in einigen Marktsegmenten hoch, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit dem Boom rund um Künstliche Intelligenz. Als weitere Herausforderungen nannte Michaud die Fragmentierung des europäischen Bankenmarktes sowie Cyberrisiken. Die EBA arbeite deshalb daran, Meldepflichten und regulatorische Vorgaben zu vereinfachen, um die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit der Banken zu stärken. Dabei gehe es nicht um geringere Kapitalanforderungen, sondern um einen effizienteren Regulierungsrahmen, betonte er.

item.description: Kenya has recorded its first confirmed Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who has been living in Democratic Republic of Congo and arrived in Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya has recorded its first confirmed Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who has been living in Democratic Republic of Congo and arrived in Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale said. The patient has since died, and 28 contacts have been identified so far including family members and health workers, Duale told a press conference. Congo has been battling its [USN:L8N43X0QI TEXT:"largest-ever"] Ebola outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo species. The outbreak was declared in mid-May but may have started months earlier and has so far resisted containment efforts, with the Central African country recording more than 8,000 cases and over [USN:L1N45O094 TEXT:"4,000 deaths"]. The outbreak earlier spread to Uganda, which reported 20 cases and two deaths, but the World Health Organization declared Uganda [USN:L6N44N0VL TEXT:"free of the disease"] in August. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, living or dead. It can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding.

item.title: UK construction activity falls at slowest pace since January
item.description: British construction activity fell further in September, but the decline was the smallest since January as a sharp downturn in housebuilding eased slightly, an industry survey showed on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: David Milliken
item.content:encoded: British construction activity fell further in September, but the decline was the smallest since January as a sharp downturn in housebuilding eased slightly, an industry survey showed on Tuesday. The S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index for Britain's construction sector rose to an eight-month high of 46.1 in September from 44.3 in August but remained well below the 50 mark that divides growth from contraction, as it has been since January 2025. "Total new orders were relatively subdued in September as construction firms reported longer sales conversion cycles and clients deferred decision-making on major projects," Tim Moore, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said. The new orders balance fell to a three-month low of 45.9 from 47.7, due to a mix of subdued demand, geopolitical tensions and rising input costs Input prices rose at their slowest rate since the outbreak of the Iran war in February, but Moore said this appeared unlikely to last due to higher energy costs Firms' expectations for future activity were the weakest since May The most recent official data showed British construction output was 1.0% lower than a year earlier in Q2 2026 Housebuilding remained the weakest sector in the PMI, followed by civil engineering, while commercial work showed only a small decline S&P Global said their all-sector PMI, which includes PMI data for [USN:ZRN00EN1B TEXT:"services"], [USN:L8N45M1O7 TEXT:"manufacturing"] and construction, slipped to a three-month low of 51.5 in September from 51.8

item.title: Most Gulf markets gain as oil-supply worries ease, Fed hike bets recede
item.description: Most major Gulf stock markets opened higher on Tuesday, supported by easing concerns over oil supplies, reduced expectations of a near-term US interest rate hike and improving global risk sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Most major Gulf stock markets opened higher on Tuesday, supported by easing concerns over oil supplies, reduced expectations of a near-term US interest rate hike and improving global risk sentiment. Data [USN:L6N45Q03T TEXT:"showed"] Gulf oil flows excluding Iran surged to over 81% of pre-war levels in September, led by a recovery in Saudi exports. The recovery came despite attacks on the kingdom's oil infrastructure and a wave of Iranian strikes on regional shipping. Iran's own exports, meanwhile, fell to zero under a US blockade. Saudi Arabia stocks led the gains, with the benchmark index (.TASI) up 0.4%. Al Rajhi Bank (1120.SE) rose 0.6% and oil giant Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) climbed 1%. Developments in Yemen also supported sentiment. Saudi Arabia said Saudi-backed Yemeni forces advanced on Monday to [USN:L1N45R06H TEXT:"recapture"] coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait up to the port city of Mocha, pushing Iran-aligned Houthi forces out of most areas seized last month. Elsewhere in the region, gains were small. The Qatari index (.QSI) added 0.2% and Dubai's main share index (.DFMGI) edged up 0.1%. US data added to the upbeat mood. Bets on a US rate hike in October faded after data released on Friday showed job growth slowed more than expected in September, while nonfarm payrolls for the previous two months were revised lower. Traders have not given up on tightening, however. CME's FedWatch Tool shows an 87% chance of a rate increase in December. Gulf markets tend to track shifts in US monetary policy expectations as most regional currencies are pegged to the dollar. Abu Dhabi bucked the regional trend, with its stock index (.FTFADGI) down 0.1%.

item.title: Recordati ferma a 53 euro, nuovo prezzo offerta, per broker non ancora sufficiente
item.description: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sull'andamento della Borsa di Milano:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sull'andamento della Borsa di Milano: 10.25 - Recordati (RECI.MI) si muove inchiodata a 53 euro (+1,4%), nuovo prezzo dell'offerta lanciata da Respighi Bidco, ritoccata oggi al rialzo rispetto ai 51,29 euro precedenti. A oggi Respighi detiene il 49,79% del capitale dell'azienda farmaceutica e secondo le stime di Equita, "con gli acquisti di azioni e derivati, detiene oltre il 59% del capitale". Per il broker, "il nuovo prezzo dell'offerta resta al di sotto della richiesta dei fondi attivisti guidati da Palliser, che ha di recente scritto al board chiedendo di alzare il prezzo a 60 euro". Anche Banca Akros ritiene l'incremento del prezzo di offerta "ancora non sufficiente per compensare adeguatamente gli azionisti di minoranza per il valore di Recordati standalone e il potenziale di crescita". Secondo il broker, il nuovo prezzo di 53 euro non è attraente relativamente alla valutazione sui fondamentali della società". 9.55 - Technoprobe balza del 4% a 37,3 euro, sui massimi da fine giugno, dopo che Jp Morgan ha avviato la copertura con la raccomandazione di 'overweight' e prezzo obiettivo a 45 euro. Secondo il broker, l'azienda che progetta e produce sonde card e tecnologie di misura per circuiti integrati è "leader di mercato" in questo settore e "per soddisfare la crescente domanda, l'azienda sta ampliando la propria capacità produttiva". Jp Morgan si attende una crescita di ricavi e utili sopra le attuali attese del mercato al 2028. 9.15 - Avvio di seduta con gli indici decisamente positivi a Piazza Affari sulla scia del balzo delle borse asiatiche trainate dal rally del Nasdaq. L'indice Ftse Mib (.FTMIB) guadagna l'1,14%. In luce le banche con l'indice settoriale che avanza dell'1,4%, trainato dalle big UNICREDIT (CRDI.MI) a +1,9% e INTESA (ISP.MI) a +1,3%. Dopo il crollo di ieri, parziale rimbalzo oggi per la controllata di MPS (BMPS.MI) (+1,4%) MEDIOBANCA (MDBI.MI) che avanza di poco sopra l'1%. RECORDATI (RECI.MI) sale dell'1,5% a 53 euro, il nuovo prezzo dell'offerta di Respighi Bidco che stamani ha annunciato un ritocco al rialzo rispetto al precedente 51,29 euro per azione, estendendo il periodo di offerta al 23 ottobre. Denaro anche su TECHNOPROBE (TPRO.MI) che balza del 4,2% a 37,36 euro dopo che Jp Morgan ha avviato la copertura con 'overweight' e target price a 45 euro. Corre DIASORIN (DIAS.MI) a +4,4%.

item.title: Spain expected to approve housing decrees that triggered snap election
item.description: Spain's government is set to approve on Tuesday two housing decrees whose rejection by parliament last week prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap election, Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain's government is set to approve on Tuesday two housing decrees whose [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"rejection by parliament"] last week prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"to call a snap election"], Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun said. The decrees will then be sent for approval by a reduced body of caretaker lawmakers who remain in place after parliament was dissolved ahead of the November 29 election, state broadcaster TVE said. The standing body of 69 members, when including lower house speaker Francina Armengol from Sanchez's Socialist Party, has a slim majority in favour of the measures, which include rent caps, a temporary ban on evictions and limits on corporate purchases of residential property, according to state broadcaster TVE. The decrees would be implemented temporarily until a new parliament is formed, TVE said. Urtasun told reporters on Monday the decrees would have some small variations but no major changes compared to those approved by the cabinet but rejected by parliament last week. "In terms of protection, they will certainly be on a par with, or even exceed, what we agreed last time," Urtasun said. Sanchez, who will hold a press conference after the cabinet meeting, said on Monday he needed more seats in parliament after failing to garner enough support for his proposals to address a [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"housing crisis"] that has drawn nationwide protests following the [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"attempted eviction"] of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid.

item.title: Former German spy chief detained on suspicion of espionage and treason, Bild reports
item.description: Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning has been detained on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, Bild newspaper reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning has been detained on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, Bild newspaper reported on Tuesday. The report said prosecutors allege Hanning, whose tenure ended in 2005, bought secret information from a former employee of the foreign intelligence agency BND and intended to sell it on as part of his consulting activities. The BND and the office of Germany's federal prosecutor did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The investigation was launched after the discovery of an alleged leak of intelligence reports intended for the chancellery, Bild said.

item.title: Francia, mercato bond non necessita intervento Bce - ministro Finanze
item.description: Le turbolenze sul mercato obbligazionario francese non hanno ancora raggiunto un livello tale da indurre a prendere in considerazione il ricorso al Transmission Protection Instrument (Tpi), lo strumento di protezione del meccanismo di trasmissione della Banca centrale europea per stabilizzare le condizioni di finanziamento.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le turbolenze sul mercato obbligazionario francese non hanno ancora raggiunto un livello tale da indurre a prendere in considerazione il ricorso al Transmission Protection Instrument (Tpi), lo strumento di protezione del meccanismo di trasmissione della Banca centrale europea per stabilizzare le condizioni di finanziamento. Lo ha detto oggi il ministro delle Finanze Roland Lescure. "L’obiettivo, ovviamente, è evitare a tutti i costi di arrivare a quel punto. Ecco perché al momento stiamo puntando sul consolidamento finanziario", ha detto Lescure ai giornalisti. Il Tpi consente alla Bce di acquistare un numero illimitato di titoli di Stato da qualsiasi Paese della zona euro che sperimenti un inasprimento "ingiustificato e disordinato" delle proprie condizioni di finanziamento.

item.title: Mistral CEO says new AI model beats Chinese ones in some areas
item.description: French AI company Mistral's newest model outperforms Chinese models on cybersecurity, CEO Arthur Mensch told a conference in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, adding the product would be unveiled later in the day.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: French AI company Mistral's newest model outperforms Chinese models on cybersecurity, CEO Arthur Mensch told a conference in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, adding the product would be unveiled later in the day. "The model we're actually announcing today is actually above the Chinese models on certain aspects, including cyber. So the narrative that Europe cannot compete is something that is not true," Mensch said onstage, without specifying which Chinese models or by what measure Mistral's model beat them. The 3-year-old company is seen as Europe's best contender in the AI race, but is still dwarfed by US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as facing pressure from [USN:L8N43M04P TEXT:"lower-cost Chinese rivals"]. Mistral, which raised €3 billion at a €21 billion valuation in a funding round [USN:L6N44Z0PP TEXT:"in September"], has sought to differentiate itself from competitors by presenting itself as a safer, European alternative. It last launched a model in April. Speaking at the Ai Everything conference, Mensch said that Mistral's independence from the US and China was enabling it to grow quickly in the Gulf and APAC region. "There's an enormous desire and an enormous need for alternative technology suppliers," he said.

item.title: インタビュー：個人向け国債「桁違い」に拡大する必要＝自民・中西氏
item.description:
Makiko Yamazaki Takaya Yamaguchi
［東京 ６日 ロイター］ - 自民党の中西健治議員は...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インタビュー：個人向け国債「桁違い」に拡大する必要＝自民・中西氏 17:27 配信

写真は円紙幣のイメージ。2022年11月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Makiko Yamazaki　Takaya Yamaguchi

［東京　６日　ロイター］ - 自民党の中西健治議員は６日、国債発行全体に占める個人向け販売を「桁違い」に拡大する必要があると述べた。税優遇を含む商品設計の見直しを通じ、国債消化の柱のひとつに据える考えを強調した。ロイターとのインタビューで語った。

財務省が６日発表した１０月発行分の個人向け国債（１０年変動、５年固定、３年固定）は１兆０２５１億円だった。

年度ベースでは累計６兆１６４１億円となり、当初計画（５兆９０００億円）をすでに上回った。過去最大だった２５年度（７兆２７１２億円）を上回るペースにある。

ただ、中西氏は「もっと買ってもらえる余地はある」と強調。「そのための後押しは必要」との考えを述べた。

日銀が国債買い入れを減らす中、２０００兆円を超える家計の金融資産をどう取り込むかは、今後の財政運営を占う試金石となる。金利上昇に伴う個人向け国債の売れ行きは好調だが、保有比率は依然として低い。

中西氏はインタビューで、税優遇を含む商品設計の見直しにも言及。利回り曲線が傾斜化し、超長期債利回りが「魅力的な水準になってきている。（１０年を超える）長いものも、あったらいい」としている。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米政府、借り入れコスト抑制へ選択肢狭まる　歳出削減以外ならインフレ加速も 焦点：仏国債下落がユーロ安に波及、選挙年控えＥＣＢの対応に注目 コラム：個人向け国債は現実的か、待機資金の流出を抑える一手とは＝唐鎌大輔氏 コラム：圧勝の高市自民党、日本トリプル高となるための条件＝高島修氏 アングル：自民圧勝に円債市場は冷静、米国の「視線」意識　政策は抑制的の思惑 最終更新: 10/6(火) 17:27 ロイター

item.title: Software startup Vinci raises $250 million at a $1.5 billion valuation
item.description: Software startup Vinci said on Tuesday it raised $250 million at a $1.5 billion valuation and is seeking to expand its suite of software used to simulate elements of chip and other hardware design.
item.dc:creator: Max Cherney
item.content:encoded: Software startup Vinci said on Tuesday it raised $250 million at a $1.5 billion valuation and is seeking to expand its suite of software used to simulate elements of chip and other hardware design. The Palo Alto, California-based company is entering a market that includes similar AI-based simulation products from established chip design software firms such as Cadence (CDNS.O) and Synopsys (SNPS.O) . Vinci's software is capable of high-fidelity physics simulation that is useful for chip and hardware designers — AI chips generate enormous amounts of heat — as the systems get larger and more complex. The company began by focusing on thermal simulation for chips but is looking to expand to help simulate whole systems. "If you ask anybody, what they are interested in — they want higher and higher fidelity physics simulation," Vinci CEO Hardik Kabaria said in an interview. The 70-person startup plans to use the proceeds from the funding round to pay for its computing costs, hire more staff and continue expanding its range of simulation products. Eventually Vinci plans to expand to other types of physics simulation like vibration testing and electromagnetics. "It is a foundation model that is proven to work in the field, so now it's about scaling up the operations and that means not just two pilot deployments but 20," Kabaria said, referring to the foundation AI model the company built to assist with the simulations. Advent, Temasek and Xora Innovation led the funding round. Venture firms Eclipse, Khosla Ventures and Madrona also participated, the company said.

item.title: Equinor CEO says Rosebank, Jackdaw rejection would be major setback
item.description: Failure to secure approval for the Rosebank and Jackdaw projects would be a major setback for Equinor's Adura joint venture with Shell in the North Sea, Equinor CEO Anders Opedal said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Failure to secure approval for the Rosebank and Jackdaw projects would be a major setback for Equinor's (EQNR.OL) Adura joint venture with Shell (SHEL.L) in the North Sea, Equinor CEO Anders Opedal said on Tuesday. "Not approving Rosebank would be contradictory to energy security, to job creation," Opedal told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London. He added that a rejection would prompt Equinor and other investors to question whether Britain remained an attractive place to invest. Rosebank and Jackdaw have become focal points for climate activists in Britain. Greenpeace and Uplift successfully challenged the projects in court over their treatment of downstream emissions, overturning the original approvals and forcing fresh applications in 2025. Britain approved Rosebank in 2023 and Jackdaw in 2022 under the previous Conservative government. A decision on Jackdaw could come within days after media reports said an announcement had been delayed until after an October 8 by-election. Much of the infrastructure needed for Jackdaw is already in place, meaning the gas field could begin production this winter if approved. Rosebank could deliver first oil in the first half of 2027. Equinor and Shell rebranded their UK North Sea joint venture as Adura in 2025. The venture is set to become the largest oil and gas producer in the UK North Sea.

item.title: Indonesia court to rule on bid to annul vice president's election win
item.description: Plaintiffs led by a former Indonesian deputy law minister filed a petition last month, arguing that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's overseas education credentials did not satisfy Indonesian eligibility requirements.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Indonesia court to rule on bid to annul vice president's election win

Plaintiffs led by a former Indonesian deputy law minister filed a petition last month, arguing that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's overseas education credentials did not satisfy Indonesian eligibility requirements.

FAST

JAKARTA: Indonesia's Constitutional Court will issue a ruling late on Tuesday (Oct 6) on a case that seeks to annul Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's election win because of alleged gaps in his education record, a move that could see him lose office and further undermine President Prabowo Subianto's administration.

Prabowo became the eighth president of Southeast Asia's largest economy after a successful but often controversial election campaign alongside Gibran, the 39-year-old eldest son of Prabowo's predecessor, Joko Widodo.

Last month, plaintiffs led by a former Indonesian deputy law minister filed a petition to the court asking its nine-judge panel to annul Gibran's vice presidency, arguing that his overseas education credentials did not satisfy Indonesian eligibility requirements and were improperly accepted by election authorities.

Indonesian election law requires presidential and vice-presidential candidates to have completed senior high school or an equivalent level of education. Plaintiffs argued Gibran failed to adequately prove he had met the criteria.

Judges are scheduled to deliver their verdict on Tuesday after holding several hearings with experts, diplomatic attaches, and the education ministry, the court's website shows.

The challenge hinges on whether Gibran's overseas studies met the requirements and whether election officials were justified in relying on government-issued equivalency certificates to support his candidacy.

Gibran attended Orchid Park Secondary School in Singapore and later studied at UTS Insearch in Australia before obtaining a bachelor's degree through the Management Development Institute of Singapore (MDIS).

Indonesian education ministry official Taufiq Damarjati told the court on Oct 2 that the ministry's equivalency assessment was based on Gibran's overall educational history, while acknowledging that no diploma was submitted during the application process, court transcripts show.

Prabowo has replaced several senior officials, including the national police chief and the Coordinating Minister for Human Development and Culture, local media reported, moves widely seen as a reflection of strains in his relationship with Widodo.

Widodo threw his support behind Prabowo, his former defence minister, during the presidential campaign.

A controversial 2023 ruling by the Constitutional Court exempted Gibran from age restrictions, paving the way for his candidacy. The move sparked protests and criticism from students, activists and legal scholars, with analysts saying it allowed Widodo to retain influence even after leaving office.

item.title: Finanzminister: Frankreich derzeit kein Fall für ein EZB-Notprogramm
item.description: Trotz der Turbulenzen am französischen Anleihemarkt sieht die Regierung in Paris Frankreich zurzeit nicht als einen Fall für ein Eingreifen der Europäischen Zentralbank. Die Turbulenzen hätten noch kein Ausmaß erreicht, das Überlegungen zum Einsatz des Notfallinstruments der EZB erforderlich machen würde, erklärte Finanzminister Roland Lescure am Dienstag. "Das Ziel ist natürlich, diesen Punkt unter allen Umständen zu vermeiden. Deshalb setzen wir derzeit auf Haushaltskonsolidierung", sagte er vor Journalisten.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Trotz der Turbulenzen am französischen Anleihemarkt sieht die Regierung in Paris Frankreich zurzeit nicht als einen Fall für ein Eingreifen der Europäischen Zentralbank. Die Turbulenzen hätten noch kein Ausmaß erreicht, das Überlegungen zum Einsatz des Notfallinstruments der EZB erforderlich machen würde, erklärte Finanzminister Roland Lescure am Dienstag. "Das Ziel ist natürlich, diesen Punkt unter allen Umständen zu vermeiden. Deshalb setzen wir derzeit auf Haushaltskonsolidierung", sagte er vor Journalisten. Am Bondmarkt zogen die Renditen vieler europäischer Staatsanleihen jüngst deutlich an. An den Finanzmärkten ist besonders Frankreich wegen seiner Haushaltsprobleme und eines schwächeren Wirtschaftswachstums zuletzt immer stärker in den Fokus geraten. Die EZB hat mit dem Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI) ein Notprogramm in der Hinterhand, mit dem sie theoretisch unbegrenzt Staatsanleihen eines in Bedrängnis geratenen Euro-Landes kaufen kann. Bedingung dafür ist aber, dass dieser Staat unter einer ungerechtfertigten Verschärfung seiner Finanzierungsbedingungen leidet und der Anstieg der Renditen ungeordnet erfolgt, beispielsweise wegen heftiger Turbulenzen an den Börsen. "Wenn es zum Schwur kommen sollte, wird die EZB vermutlich mit dem TPI-Instrument eingreifen", meint Cyrus de la Rubia, Chefvolkswirt der Hamburg Commercial Bank. Das gelte insbesondere dann, wenn andere Länder wie Italien, Spanien und Portugal angesteckt würden. Erste Bewegungen in diese Richtung ließen sich schon beobachten: "Bislang kann man allerdings noch nicht erkennen, dass Frankreich und den anderen Ländern der Zugang zum Kapitalmarkt verwehrt wird", so der Experte.

item.title: Domestic banks tighten grip on equity deals as fundraising surges
item.description: Kotak Mahindra Capital Co. reclaimed the top position after working on 45 deals through the end of September, capturing a 9.5% market share ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Rajesh Mascarenhas Domestic investment banks are grabbing the bulk of the business on India’s equity capital markets, just as dealmaking is surging in the second half of the year. Kotak Mahindra Capital Co. reclaimed the top position after working on 45 deals through the end of September, capturing a 9.5% market share. While Goldman Sachs Group Inc. ranked second, the highest among Wall Street giants, Indian banks together claimed seven of the top 10 spots in the league table, their strongest showing in eight years. With three months of the year still to go, the standings may yet change substantially as the fourth quarter is traditionally the busiest in India. Equity dealmaking has accelerated after a subdued start to the year, helped by a string of large share sales. Life Insurance Corp. of India, National Stock Exchange of India Ltd., Adani Enterprises Ltd., SBI Funds Management Ltd. and Manipal Health Enterprises Ltd. together raised over $9 billion, providing a boost to issuance. Jefferies Group LLC and Citigroup Inc. were the only other foreign firms to make the top 10, at fifth and sixth, respectively. JPMorgan Chase & Co., which topped India’s equity league table last year, fell to 12th. Among local banks, IIFL Capital Services Ltd. surged to third place after working on 37 transactions, while ICICI Securities Ltd. took fourth place with 43 deals.  Domestic banks last dominated the top of the league table in a similar fashion in 2018. Their resurgence is another sign of the local financial industry’s growing power. India’s institutional investors increasingly provide the backbone for local equity markets, helping domestic investment banks win a bigger share of underwriting mandates even as overseas investors retreat from stocks. “This year’s ECM activity has been dominated by IPOs and share sales by state-owned companies, giving domestic investment banks an edge in winning mandates,” said V. Jayasankar, managing director and co-chief executive officer, Kotak Investment Banking Ltd. “Their deep relationships with Indian issuers and local investors have further strengthened their position, particularly as foreign portfolio investors remain relatively cautious.” Indian funds are also increasingly driving valuations for initial public offerings as they exert their pricing power to push for discounts that reflect the broader equity market’s struggles.  Foreign institutional investors have sold more than $30 billion of Indian shares so far in 2026, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, have bought about $68 billion, National Securities Depository Ltd. data show. The pipeline remains crowded. Jio Platforms Ltd. is preparing a proposed share sale of more than $3.1 billion, while Avaada Electro Ltd. is planning an IPO of about $800 million. Advanta Enterprises Ltd. is also weighing an offering that could raise as much as $400 million.

item.title: Londres podría expulsar a diplomáticos israelíes si se cierra el consulado de Jerusalén, dicen fuentes
item.description: Es probable que Reino Unido expulse a diplomáticos israelíes si Israel lleva a cabo esta semana su orden de cerrar el consulado británico en Jerusalén Este, en el marco de una disputa sobre las sanciones dirigidas contra los asentamientos israelíes, según cuatro fuentes.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: Es probable que Reino Unido expulse a diplomáticos israelíes si Israel lleva a cabo esta semana su orden de cerrar el consulado británico en Jerusalén Este, en el marco de una disputa sobre las sanciones dirigidas contra los asentamientos israelíes, según cuatro fuentes. El 8 de septiembre, Israel ordenó a Reino Unido que cerrara el consulado de Jerusalén Este en un plazo de 30 días y retirara a sus diplomáticos de la ciudad, después de que Reino Unido anunciara que impondría una prohibición al comercio de productos fabricados en los asentamientos israelíes del territorio bajo ocupación israelí de Cisjordania. El plazo de 30 días para que Reino Unido cierre el consulado finaliza el jueves, lo que afectará a unos 30 diplomáticos británicos que trabajan allí, así como a sus familiares, según las fuentes. Si se cierra el consulado, es probable que Reino Unido responda expulsando a un número similar de diplomáticos israelíes de la embajada de Israel en Reino Unido, según las fuentes, que hablaron bajo condición de anonimato. Las fuentes no precisaron con qué rapidez actuaría Reino Unido en caso de que se cerrara el consulado. Tras el anuncio de las sanciones por la parte británica, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores israelí, Gideon Saar, acusó a Londres de interferir en las elecciones generales israelíes de este mes. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores británico no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores israelí se negó a hacer declaraciones. Un funcionario israelí dijo que cualquier medida contra Israel recibiría una respuesta. El anuncio de las sanciones británicas y la respuesta de Israel marcaron un nuevo punto bajo en la relación entre los que en su día fueron aliados inquebrantables. Reino Unido ha criticado repetidamente a Israel por sus acciones en la guerra de Gaza y por los ataques de colonos israelíes contra palestinos. El Gobierno de Israel ha acusado al Partido Laborista, actualmente en el poder en Reino Unido, de mostrarse hostil hacia Israel. El consulado británico, situado en el barrio de Sheij Yarrah, en Jerusalén Este, se encarga de las relaciones del país con los palestinos tanto en la ciudad como en Cisjordania y Gaza. También presta servicios consulares a los palestinos. El consulado lleva casi 200 años en Jerusalén. El Estado de Israel se fundó en 1948. Reuters informó el lunes de que el principal asesor de seguridad nacional británico, Jonathan Powell, había visitado discretamente Israel la semana pasada con el objetivo de mantener abierto el consulado, pero no logró alcanzar un acuerdo. Una quinta fuente dijo que Reino Unido aún tenía esperanzas de que se pudiera llegar a un acuerdo. Otras dos fuentes indicaron que Reino Unido ha pedido a los países europeos que planteen la cuestión a Israel con la esperanza de convencer al Gobierno de que revierta su decisión. Un portavoz del ministro de Asuntos Exteriores israelí, Gideon Saar, declaró el lunes a Reuters que el consulado cerraría el jueves. Al anunciar las sanciones, Reino Unido afirmó que las acciones de Israel estaban socavando la posibilidad de una solución de dos Estados, la idea de un Estado palestino que coexista pacíficamente junto a Israel. El Gobierno del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu rechaza abiertamente la idea de un Estado palestino. Reino Unido, que reconoció al Estado de Palestina el año pasado, señaló los proyectos respaldados por el Gobierno israelí para ampliar los asentamientos y el aumento de los ataques de los colonos contra los palestinos en Cisjordania. Las sanciones británicas entrarán en vigor el año que viene. Francia y Canadá se sumaron al anuncio de sanciones. Israel no ha tomado medidas contra París ni Ottawa. El incidente puso de manifiesto la creciente frustración entre los aliados históricos de Israel por sus asentamientos en Cisjordania ocupada, territorio que Israel conquistó en la guerra de 1967. Casi todos los países y todos los órganos de la ONU consideran que los asentamientos son ilegales según el derecho internacional, algo que Israel niega.

item.title: UK PM weighs delay to roadmap for higher defence spending, Times reports
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering delaying an announcement on how and when Britain will raise defence spending to 3% of GDP, The Times reported on Tuesday, pushing back a key milestone on the path to meeting NATO's target of 3.5% by 2035.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister [USN:L8N45K17W TEXT:"Andy Burnham"] is considering delaying an announcement on how and when Britain will raise defence spending to 3% of GDP, The Times reported on Tuesday, pushing back a key milestone on the path to meeting NATO's target of 3.5% by 2035. Britain is [USN:L1N42D0AX TEXT:"under pressure"] to spell out how it will meet the NATO commitment and respond to a heightened security threat. Burnham has [USN:L8N45J05G TEXT:"pledged"] to meet the 2035 target, but his government has yet to set out the steps required to get there. Finance minister John Healey said earlier this year he would outline an initial path to 3% of GDP at the next spending review, which was expected in spring 2027. The Times cited a source as saying the "working assumption" was that the review would take place in October 2027. A spokesperson for the finance ministry said it was wrong talk of a delay. "The date of the Spending Review has not been set. This is pure rumour and speculation," the spokesperson said in an email. Highlighting the security challenges facing Britain, the US on Sunday [USN:L1N45R04X TEXT:"removed bombers"] from an airbase in England after it was targeted in a suspected Iranian plot. Ministers have repeatedly delayed decisions on additional defence funding over the past two years. Healey, finance minister since July, [USN:L8N42J0TA TEXT:"resigned"] as defence minister in the previous government after failing to secure funding to raise defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030, a move that helped bring down then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer. According to the Office for Budget Responsibility, reaching that interim goal would cost the government an additional £17.3 billion ($22.9 billion). To meet the needs of the existing Defence Investment Plan, Healey needs to fill a £4.7 billion funding gap. Healey is due to deliver his first budget on October 28. ($1 = 0.7559 pounds)

item.title: Lithuania says it would pay the cost if US establishes military base
item.description: Lithuania is ready to pay the cost to set up a permanent US military base if Washington should agree to establish one there, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lithuania is ready to pay the cost to set up a permanent US military base if Washington should agree to establish one there, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said on Tuesday. On Monday, US President Donald Trump said [USN:S0N43J05I TEXT:"he would consider"] Lithuania's request for a permanent base: "They are friends of mine, they are great people, so we will certainly look at it." Lithuania, a member of the EU and NATO, borders Russia and Moscow's close ally Belarus. The United States has kept an armoured battalion of almost 1,000 troops there since 2019, in overlapping rotations, meaning the troops arrive and leave every few months. Sinkevicius said he proposed turning this into a permanent presence at a meeting with Trump's envoy John Coale last month in Vilnius. "I'm glad that this idea is being taken seriously... This is a critically important guarantee of deterrence and security," Sinkevicius wrote on Facebook. "Our partners only need to make the political decision to permanently station troops, and Lithuania is ready to cover the costs involved."

item.title: ECB's Rehn: High yields to dampen energy price pass-through
item.description: Rapid energy inflation across the euro zone has not yet spread to other goods and services, and the recent rise in bond yields is likely to dampen price pressures as it weighs on growth, European Central Bank policymaker Olli Rehn said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rapid energy inflation across the euro zone has not yet spread to other goods and services, and the recent rise in bond yields is likely to dampen price pressures as it weighs on growth, European Central Bank policymaker Olli Rehn said on Tuesday. Euro zone inflation is now running well above the ECB’s 2% target, and policymakers are debating just how much more they need to hike rates on top of the two moves this past summer. While a host of policymakers have said that inflation risks are tilted to higher readings than predicted, Rehn said there were other considerations, too, as opposing forces were at work in the economy. "The rise in long-term interest rates is contributing to a slowdown in growth and also to a reduction in the pass-through of energy prices to other prices and to wages," says Rehn said, echoing some of ECB chief economist [USN:L1N45R07O TEXT:"Philip Lane's comments"]. ECB board member [USN:L1N45M0QP TEXT:"Isabel Schnabel"], an outspoken policy hawk, has also warned recently that the economy could respond more to surging borrowing costs more strongly than assumed, which would dampen medium-term inflationary pressures. Yields have risen to more than decade highs across the bloc, partly as they follow U.S. yields higher and partly because of increased debt sustainability concerns in Europe. Rehn, however, stopped short of advocating a policy step and instead stuck very closely to the ECB's recent policy of not signalling moves ahead of decisions. Financial markets see two to three more rate hikes from the ECB in the current cycle, including an 80% chance of a move by December. Rehn also acknowledged that energy prices are high and the economy is proving exceptionally resilient, partly on strong investment into artificial intelligence, Rehn added. This resilience, some policymakers have said, suggests more price pressures than earlier thought.

item.title: Ifo Institut: Mehrheit für verpflichtende Maßnahmen in frühkindlicher Bildung
item.description: Angesichts der auch im Pisa-Test zutage getretenen Lerndefizite bei Schülern ist eine deutliche Mehrheit der Deutschen für mehr verpflichtende Maßnahmen bei frühkindlicher Bildung. Insgesamt 72 Prozent halten ein verpflichtendes Vorschuljahr für geboten, 79 Prozent wollen bundesweit einheitliche verbindliche Bildungsziele, wie aus dem am Dienstag veröffentlichten "Ifo-Bildungsbarometer 2026" hervorgeht. Eine überwältigende Mehrheit (89 Prozent) stimmt zudem für verpflichtende Sprachtests im Alter von viereinhalb Jahren: "Frühkindliche Bildung legt wichtige Grundlagen für die kognitive, sprachliche, soziale und emotionale Entwicklung von Kindern", sagte Ludger Wößmann, Leiter des Ifo-Zentrums für Bildungsökonomik. Deshalb sei eine qualitativ hochwertige frühkindliche Bildung für alle Kinder wichtig.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Angesichts der auch im Pisa-Test zutage getretenen Lerndefizite bei Schülern ist eine deutliche Mehrheit der Deutschen für mehr verpflichtende Maßnahmen bei frühkindlicher Bildung. Insgesamt 72 Prozent halten ein verpflichtendes Vorschuljahr für geboten, 79 Prozent wollen bundesweit einheitliche verbindliche Bildungsziele, wie aus dem am Dienstag veröffentlichten "Ifo-Bildungsbarometer 2026" hervorgeht. Eine überwältigende Mehrheit (89 Prozent) stimmt zudem für verpflichtende Sprachtests im Alter von viereinhalb Jahren: "Frühkindliche Bildung legt wichtige Grundlagen für die kognitive, sprachliche, soziale und emotionale Entwicklung von Kindern", sagte Ludger Wößmann, Leiter des Ifo-Zentrums für Bildungsökonomik. Deshalb sei eine qualitativ hochwertige frühkindliche Bildung für alle Kinder wichtig. Die internationale OECD-Vergleichsstudie [USN:L8N45014H TEXT:"Pisa"] zeigte jüngst, dass 2025 die Durchschnittsergebnisse deutscher Schüler in Mathematik und Lesekompetenz niedriger waren als 2022. Deutschland nimmt seit 2000 an dem Test teil und nie zuvor waren die Ergebnisse schlechter. Angesichts dieser historisch schlechten Resultate dringen auch Fachleute, sowie [USN:L8N45D17U TEXT:"Arbeitgeber und Gewerkschaften"] auf bessere Bildung und plädieren vor allem für einen weiteren Ausbau der Kindertagesbetreuung. Um mehr Kita-Fachkräfte zu gewinnen, befürworten die Befragten im Ifo-Bildungsbarometer eine höhere Bezahlung des Personals und weniger bürokratischen Aufwand. Große Mehrheiten sind für mehr Männer und Quereinsteiger unter den Kita-Fachkräften. "Etwa drei Viertel der Befragten sind zudem für steigende Ausgaben für Kitas", erläuterte Ifo-Forscherin Vera Freundl. Für das Bildungsbarometer wurden im Mai und Juni 3033 Personen im Alter zwischen 18 und 69 Jahren sowie 965 Eltern mit Kindern im Alter von bis zu sechs Jahren in Deutschland repräsentativ befragt.

item.title: Fast-track permits turn Spain's Aragon into a $70 billion data centre magnet. At what cost?
item.description: Aragon, a sparsely populated region of northeast Spain, has become one of Europe's fastest-growing digital infrastructure hubs due to what tech companies hail as its agile local permitting laws and swift decision making.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Lombardi, Corina Pons
item.content:encoded: Aragon, a sparsely populated region of northeast Spain, has become one of Europe's fastest-growing digital infrastructure hubs due to what tech companies hail as its agile local permitting laws and swift decision making. Located at the crossroads of major international cable connections, Aragon offers abundant renewable energy and land, and is set to see more than €60 billion ($67.55 billion) of investment in data centres and digital infrastructure in the next decade. A dozen company officials, experts and campaigners told Reuters that the most decisive factor drawing investment to the region is its data centre–friendly governance. Big tech companies believe Aragon could serve as a model for a European Union [USN:L6N45D0CN TEXT:"seeking"] to triple its data centre capacity within seven years, and narrow the AI infrastructure gap with the US and China. However, [USN:L4N44F1BQ TEXT:"global concerns"] over data centres' resource consumption, environmental impact and burden on local communities are growing, and Spain's national government is seeking to impose new resource requirements. STREAMLINING A COMPLEX PROCESS In Aragon, the regional government defends its strategy. "Are we overlooking any requirements for the sake of speed? The answer is no," said Eva Valle, Aragon's economy minister. "We're simply streamlining a process that can be very complex. It's surprising how much time can be saved simply by bringing a little order to it." Aragon offers qualifying projects a "Project of General Interest of Aragon", or PIGA status, which brings swift planning decisions, facilitates land expropriations and local tax breaks. The region is also unique in providing a one-stop investor service that supports applications and gives companies weekly progress updates on their projects. PIGA status can cut approval times from years to under 12 months. AMAZON A HUGE INVESTOR IN ARAGON On the outskirts of Villanueva de Gallego, a small Aragonese town north of Zaragoza, hundreds of workers have been constructing Amazon Web Services' new facilities. The company is investing a total of €33.7 billion ($38.4 billion) in the region in cloud services and AI infrastructure, its largest investment of this kind outside the US. The new facilities moved through most of the permitting procedure in around a year, lightning speed for Europe's often glacial pace of infrastructure licensing. Aragon has fast-tracked over a dozen large data centre projects also for Microsoft and others, regional data shows. TOO FAST? Critics of the scheme say the fast-track process undermines public and environmental accountability. By reducing administrative procedures such as public consultation requirements, "it becomes very difficult to conduct genuine scrutiny," said Manuel Garcia, a researcher at the state-run science and technology centre CSIC. The public had just 23 days at the end of 2024 to review about 25,000 pages of Amazon project documentation and submit objections if they wished, a feat Garcia called "physiologically impossible". Environmental group Ecologistas en Accion has challenged Aragon over the fast track granted to Amazon in what is believed to be Spain's first lawsuit targeting a major data centre development. But experts say any court ruling could take years, by which time many facilities would be operational. The European Commission recently [USN:L6N45D0CN TEXT:"proposed new rules"] for data centres, including faster permitting, and received submissions from Amazon and Microsoft praising Aragon. "Based on our experience, the PIGA process in Aragon, Spain, has been successful to reduce the administrative burden on companies and most importantly the handling time, while ensuring a high compliance standard with applicable regulations," Amazon said in its submission. Microsoft pointed to Aragon as an example of a European region giving data centres "prioritized and streamlined permit application review... while still ensuring full compliance with local laws." Spanish property company Merlin Properties' €1.2 billion project is among those being fast-tracked, and its CEO Ismael Clemente said the region has "managed to be very quick." MADRID'S NEW RULES SPARK BACKLASH The push in Aragon, run by Spain's conservative opposition People's Party, coincides with growing opposition around the world to data centres due to land use, power costs and water resources. The central government, facing surging energy demands from the sector and still grappling with consequences of last year's [USN:L8N4101GA TEXT:"catastrophic blackout"], has [USN:L8N44M1HX TEXT:"drafted"] tougher water and electricity rules for data centres. These have been criticised by the industry and energy companies, as well as by Aragon's authorities, who say the measures would put multi-billion-euro investments at risk. A snap election [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"called"] for November 29 looms over the draft rules, adding a layer of uncertainty. "If the proposed decree is approved, many of the projects will surely be re-evaluated," said Alberto Nadal, People's Party deputy secretary for the economy, blaming Madrid for failing to expand the power grid. Amazon's AWS and Microsoft said their plans in the region remain unaltered. A spokesperson for AWS urged Spain to protect long-term investment by aligning data centre regulation with emerging EU [USN:L6N45D0CN TEXT:"frameworks"]. AWS has also said it will spend €30 million on local community programmes in education and sustainability for example, in areas where it is present. A spokesperson for Microsoft, which plans to invest up to €10 billion in Aragon, underlined the importance of "legal certainty, predictability and conditions" for continued long-term investment in Spain. The company also has community programmes. Judith Arnal, a senior research fellow at think tank Fedea, said data centre investment must be balanced with regional economic benefits. "We need to roll out the red carpet for data centres … but we also need to try to extract as much economic value as possible." ($1 = 0.8780 euros)

item.title: VORSCHAU Die Erbschaftsteuer auf dem Prüfstand des Bundesverfassungsgerichts
item.description: Das Bundesverfassungsgericht in Karlsruhe verhandelt in der kommenden Woche an zwei Tagen über ein hoch umstrittenes Thema: die Erbschaftsteuer. Am Montag geht es in der Klage Bayerns darum, ob der Bund überhaupt für die Erbschaftsteuer zuständig ist und sie nicht vielmehr von den einzelnen Bundesländern geregelt werden muss. Am Dienstag verhandelt der Erste Senat dann über die Erbschaftsteuer für Betriebsvermögen - genauer gesagt über die mögliche Steuerverschonung, wenn Unternehmen vererbt werden.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Das Bundesverfassungsgericht in Karlsruhe verhandelt in der kommenden Woche an zwei Tagen über ein hoch umstrittenes Thema: die Erbschaftsteuer. Am Montag geht es in der Klage Bayerns darum, ob der Bund überhaupt für die Erbschaftsteuer zuständig ist und sie nicht vielmehr von den einzelnen Bundesländern geregelt werden muss. Am Dienstag verhandelt der Erste Senat dann über die [USN:L6N45R0P1 TEXT:"Erbschaftsteuer für Betriebsvermögen"] - genauer gesagt über die mögliche Steuerverschonung, wenn Unternehmen vererbt werden. Im ersten Fall bestreitet Bayern die Gesetzgebungskompetenz des Bundes. Die Staatsregierung von CSU und Freien Wählern hält das geltende Erbschaftsteuergesetz für verfassungswidrig. Es werde nicht berücksichtigt, dass die Freibeträge für Erben bundesweit gleich seien, die Immobilienpreise je nach Region aber sehr unterschiedlich ausfielen. Außerdem seien die Freibeträge für Erben trotz Inflation nicht angepasst worden. Im Jahr 2014 entschied das Bundesverfassungsgericht, dass der Bund jedenfalls bei der Vererbung von Betrieben für die Erbschaftsteuer zuständig ist, weil sonst eine Zersplitterung der Vorschriften zu befürchten sei. Ob das Gericht die Zuständigkeit des Bundes auch bei der Erbschaftsteuer für Privatvermögen bejaht, muss der Erste Senat nun entscheiden. Der zweite Fall, der am Dienstag verhandelt wird, ist noch brisanter. Es geht um die unterschiedlich hohe Besteuerung von Betriebsvermögen einerseits und Privatvermögen andererseits. Hintergrund ist die Klage eines Mannes, der Vermögen und Grundstücke von seiner Tante erbte. Er musste wesentlich höhere Erbschaftsteuern bezahlen als ein Erbe, der denselben Wert in Form eines Betriebes geerbt hätte. Denn bei Betriebsvermögen gelten verschiedene Begünstigungen, sofern Erben den Betrieb weiterführen. Sie reichen von einer weitgehenden Steuerfreistellung bis zu einem vollständigen Erlass der Steuer. Diese Privilegierung hält der Kläger für verfassungswidrig. Ein Urteil des Bundesverfassungsgerichts ist in beiden Fällen erst in einigen Monaten zu erwarten. Es ist nicht das erste Mal, dass sich das Bundesverfassungsgericht mit der Erbschaftsteuer für Betriebsvermögen befasst. 2014 beanstandete der Erste Senat des Bundesverfassungsgerichts die Privilegierung besonders großer Betriebsvermögen bei der Erbschaftsteuer. Zwar dürfe der Bund kleinere und mittlere Unternehmen zur Sicherung ihres Bestands und der Arbeitsplätze steuerlich begünstigen, hieß es damals. Bei größeren Unternehmen sei das aber nur bei vorheriger Bedürfnisprüfung zulässig. Die damalige Große Koalition unter Angela Merkel (CDU) änderte daraufhin 2016 die Vorschriften, die nun erneut vor dem Verfassungsgericht landen. Unter den politischen Parteien ist die Erbschaftsteuer umstritten. Die SPD schlug kürzlich einen Freibetrag von 900.000 Euro für Erben vor, danach soll es weniger Ausnahmen von der Erbschaftsteuer geben. Die Union will das Urteil des Bundesverfassungsgerichts abwarten. Die AfD plädiert dafür, die Erbschaftsteuer zu streichen. Die Linke will dagegen sowohl für Privatvermögen als auch für Betriebsvermögen eine progressive Besteuerung von sechs bis 60 Prozent.

item.title: BOURSE L'Europe ouvre dans le vert, accalmie sur l'obligataire
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes avancent mardi en début de séance, soulagées par une accalmie sur le marché obligataire, tandis que les investisseurs restent attentifs à la dépréciation de l'euro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes avancent mardi en début de séance, soulagées par une accalmie sur le marché obligataire, tandis que les investisseurs restent attentifs à la dépréciation de l'euro. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) gagne 0,50% à 7.873,64 points vers 07h40 GMT. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) avance de 0,76% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) prend 0,76%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) gagne 0,73%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) 0,78% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) 0,76%. Les marchés d'actions démarrent la séance sur une note positive alors que les rendements obligataires, qui restent toutefois élevés, s'apaisent en ce début matinée, les investisseurs évaluant l'ampleur du resserrement monétaire à venir. Philip Lane, chef économiste de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), a réaffirmé mardi à l'agence de presse italienne Ansa que les coûts de l'énergie n'avaient pas encore entraîné les effets de second tour tant redoutés, ce qui contribue à rassurer les investisseurs bien que l'inflation globale avoisine les 4% dans le bloc. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans perd 5,2 points de base à 3,4391%, tandis que celui de son homologue français de même écheance abandonne 7 points de base à 4,7919%. Les investisseurs ne perdent toutefois pas de vue les difficultés budgétaires qui sapent la confiance en France à l'approche du débat budgétaire au sein d'une Assemblée nationale fragmentée et peu encline au compromis à l'approche des élections présidentielles du printemps 2027. Dans ce contexte, Roland Lescure, le ministre français de l'Economie, a dit mardi que les OAT ne subissent pas de pression due aux ventes, mais plutôt à un manque d'acheteurs. Il a également indiqué ne percevoir aucun signe de méfiance à l'égard de l'euro suite aux turbulences sur le marché obligataire français, une question qui préoccupe toutefois les investisseurs, alors que la monnaie européenne se négocie à un niveau proche de son plus bas depuis mai 2025 face au dollar. Les investisseurs font en outre abstraction des données en provenance d'Allemagne, qui montrent que les commandes industrielles ont chuté bien plus que prévu en août, et attendent la publication d'autres indicateurs au cours de la séance, notamment les ventes au détail de la zone euro. Aux valeurs, Sabadell (SABE.MC) gagne 2,48%, le groupe bancaire français BPCE [USN:L6N45S0C8 TEXT:"ayant acquis"] une participation d'environ 7% dans la banque espagnole. Les groupes pharmaceutiques se démarquent, avec Biomérieux (BIOX.PA) progressant de 4,2% et Eurofins Scientific (EUFI.PA) de 3%, les analystes soulignant la bonne performance du secteur.

item.title: インフレ二次的効果、現時点でそれほど強くない＝ＥＣＢ専務理事
item.description: [フランクフルト ６日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）チーフエコノミストのレーン専務理事はイタリアの通信社Ａ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インフレ二次的効果、現時点でそれほど強くない＝ＥＣＢ専務理事 17:02 配信

欧州中央銀行（ECB）チーフエコノミストのレーン専務理事。6月16日、ロンドンで撮影。REUTERS/Chris J. Ratcliffe

[フランクフルト ６日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）チーフエコノミストのレーン専務理事はイタリアの通信社ＡＮＳＡに対し、ユーロ圏における高いエネルギーコストはまだ二次的なインフレ効果をもたらしておらず、そうした効果の強さも不透明だと述べた。

６日に配信されたインタビューで「現時点では、それほど強い二次的効果は見られていない。引き続き注視している」と説明。「私自身はさまざまなシナリオを提唱している立場ではあるが、われわれが『悪化シナリオ』にあるとか、『基本シナリオ』にあると断言するのはあまりに短絡的だ」と語った。

「エネルギー価格は高いが、経済の他の分野への波及の強さは依然として不透明だ」と付け加えた。

item.title: Hungary to open Communist-era informer files in reckoning with Cold War past
item.description: In a historic move, Hungary will soon start releasing tens of thousands of Communist-era police files in an online public database, giving people access to lists of informers and collaborators used by the former state security services.
item.dc:creator: Krisztina Than
item.content:encoded: In a historic move, Hungary will soon start releasing tens of thousands of Communist-era police files in an online public database, giving people access to lists of informers and collaborators used by the former state security services. The release, timed for the 70th anniversary of Hungary's 1956 anti-Soviet uprising, is part of Prime Minister Peter Magyar's pledge to make the records, stored in a vast basement of archives in Budapest, public and allow Hungarians to come to terms with their totalitarian past. Although Communist rule ended in 1989, Hungary delayed fully opening the files due to a lack of strong political will from successive governments. So far, apart from researchers, ordinary people could only request access to their own records or those of close family members but now anybody will be able to conduct searches in the online database. During the Cold War, secret police agencies in eastern Europe such as East Germany's Stasi or Hungary's security services relied on collaborators drawn from the public, often via blackmail, threats or rewards. Between 1956 and 1989 some 55,000 secret collaborators were recorded in Hungary. They monitored friends, family members, neighbours and co-workers to detect signs of dissent and Western influence -- and their reports often led to arrests and interrogation. Many flats in downtown Budapest -- called K-flats or conspiracy flats -- served as locations for meetings between secret police officials and civilian collaborators. MUSIC BANDS TARGETED In the 1980s, informants attended concerts in Budapest's underground rock scene that attracted youthful crowds and were seen by the authorities as potentially subversive. Peter Muller "Sziami", still an iconic figure in today's music scene, recalls his band Kontroll Csoport (group) performing in 1983 a song he had written titled "Informers and Provocateurs". "In our own way," the lyrics read, "we keep watch too: the one standing in front of you is our man -- you’ve blushed, you’ve been exposed, informers and provocateurs." "And then we turned spotlights on the crowd and we saw the audience of around 1,000 people spinning around, looking to see who could be the informers," Muller, 74, said in his studio, smiling mischievously. Muller was almost thrown out of college for his music, and police banned some of his concerts and interrogated him. His first punk-rock band called "URH" in 1980, legendary in the underground culture, was named after the radio frequency band used by the state police and was often targeted. Despite those memories, however, Muller has mixed feelings about the opening of the files after such a long time. "I do not feel entirely comfortable with the idea that society needs such a cleansing or catharsis after all this time — that people must be singled out, humiliated, shamed, and punished when they have either already died or moved on to a different stage of life," he told Reuters. CONFRONTING OUR PAST 'MORE DEEPLY' The Historical Archives of the Hungarian State Security (ABTL) manages the former state security services' records, with files comprising the names of 50,000 to 60,000 collaborators. Its director, Bendeguz Gergo Cseh, hailed the release of the Communist-era files, based on a law passed by parliament in September, as a "historic step" and said it went further than elsewhere in the former eastern bloc. Poland opened its archives much earlier but does not allow open, unrestricted searches, as will be the case now in Hungary. Germany also took a more restrictive approach in its 1991 act to open the Stasi files, while in the Czech Republic not all files have been uploaded to an online database. The Hungarian law says understanding the past and the transparency of public institutions are "essential prerequisites" for the functioning of a democratic state. The release of four types of files will come in two stages, starting on November 4. On that day in 1956 Soviet tanks entered Budapest to crush a pro-democracy uprising that had begun on October 23. Some details of the files will be redacted to protect sensitive personal information, including health records, addictions and sexual orientation. "As both an archivist and a historian, I believe that passing judgment based on this information is inappropriate," Cseh told Reuters. "However, I do think it is possible to gain insight into life stories and confront our past more deeply — not only at an individual level but also at a societal one."
